title: Kolkata Pandal Stampede Toll Rises to 19, High Court Judge to Lead Probe
excerpt: Two more deaths were confirmed in the Chorbagan crush, taking the toll to 19 including 13 women and a child, as West Bengal sought a judge-led SIT and announced Rs 25 lakh for each bereaved family.
body:
• The death toll in the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal crush in north Kolkata has risen to 19, including 13 women and a child, with about 25 people injured and eight in critical condition.
  • West Bengal will seek a probe led by a sitting Calcutta High Court judge, heading a Special Investigation Team, after police obtained CCTV footage and detained 12 people including organisers.
  • The state announced Rs 25 lakh and a government job for each bereaved family, Rs 5 lakh for the injured, while the Centre announced Rs 2 lakh for families of the dead and Rs 50,000 for the injured.
  • State helplines for families are 1800-345-5678 and 033-22141310; the Chorbagan pandal is closed and Durga Puja continues statewide until October 21.

The death toll from the crush at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata rose to 19 on Sunday, after two more deaths were confirmed, according to The Hindu. Of the dead, 13 were women and one was a child, NDTV reported, citing police and doctors. About 25 people were injured, eight of them critical.

The increase, from the 17 deaths reported earlier, is the central new development in a tragedy that unfolded at about 7:40 p.m. on Saturday, Maha Saptami, at the pandal's exit gate in the Girish Park police station area. Seventeen people were brought dead to Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, one child died at R.G. Kar Medical College and Hospital, and another person died while being taken to a private facility, the state government said.

A judge-led investigation

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said he would write to the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court seeking the appointment of a sitting judge to oversee a Special Investigation Team probing the incident. Kolkata Police have obtained CCTV footage from the Chorbagan pandal and are questioning 12 detained people, including organisers and volunteers.

"We will check the CCTV footage to see if the crowd was being properly controlled. We will determine who is responsible: the organising committee, the police, private security, or anyone else. There's no question of sparing anyone."

— Suvendu Adhikari, West Bengal Chief Minister

According to preliminary reports cited by The Hindu, panic spread after organisers allegedly made a misleading announcement over a microphone asking people to leave, claiming the structure could collapse, while private security personnel blew whistles. Large numbers of visitors had taken shelter inside the pandal after rain began, and witnesses pointed to narrow entry and exit gates and poor lighting at the site.

Compensation and official response

The state government announced Rs 25 lakh for the next of kin of each person killed, a Group D government job for one member of each bereaved family, and Rs 5 lakh for each injured person. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who called the incident extremely distressing, announced Rs 2 lakh from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund for families of the dead and Rs 50,000 for the injured.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who was in West Bengal, postponed his scheduled programmes to visit the injured. Former chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also expressed grief and called for a thorough investigation and prompt assistance.

What happens next

The Chorbagan pandal, themed 'Arava' or 'Beyond Sound', has been closed. Adhikari also announced a high-level committee to review safety arrangements at major pandals across the state and urged organisers to ensure adequate safety and lighting for the remaining days of the festival. Around 57,400 Durga Pujas are being organised across West Bengal this year, and the festival runs until Wednesday, October 21. The judge-led probe and the CCTV review will determine whether failures lay with crowd management at the gate, the announcements that triggered the rush, or the permissions and oversight that preceded it.
